item.title: ‘Wake-up call’ for Asean energy security as Singapore, Thailand face Iran war's LNG risks
item.description: Long-term energy security is also a concern for Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam, which have been expanding LNG infrastructure. Experts say that a shift to renewables is worthwhile, but policies are diverging across the region.

item.title: Rethinking Malaysia’s path to net zero
item.description: Carbon credits to be tabled under Malaysia’s new climate change bill should serve as a bridge towards decarbonisation rather than a substitute for it.

item.title: What does the US pursuit of critical minerals mean for the Global South?
item.description: Supply-chain push may bring new deals but do little to help producer countries develop their mining sectors.

item.title: Migrant fishers’ deaths expose unchecked power at sea: study
item.description: A new study finds migrant fishers’ deaths at sea stem from systemic labour and governance failures, not isolated safety lapses.

item.title: Southeast Asia’s blue economy programmes unaffected by reported UK climate aid cuts, say project leads
item.description: The United Kingdom’s flagship £500 million Blue Planet Fund, which supports marine environment programmes in developing countries like the Philippines, Indonesia and Vietnam, is in question, following news of a planned budget cut.

item.title: AI can propel women forward – or set them back further
item.description: AI will mostly benefit those already well positioned to leverage it – men. Businesses and governments cannot afford to overlook gender as they invest in talent policies for the AI age.

item.title: Singapore outlines first national climate adaptation plan
item.description: Singapore's draft adaptation plan will address heat resilience, coastal defence, and water security. Climate scientists and NGOs say the plan must also include nature and the most vulnerable to climate risks in its design.

item.title: Middle East crisis increases Southeast Asia's coal risk
item.description: Now is the time to double down on renewable energy and electrification.

item.title: Japan firms develop low-energy process to recover ammonia from biogas waste
item.description: Technology could cut emissions and support circular nitrogen use, developers say.

item.title: China sets 17 per cent carbon intensity cut in new five-year climate plan
item.description: Beijing leans on rapid renewable expansion but sets no target for emissions decline before 2030.
